prior_art.decode: Not a DECODE item: known.py on the harvested dump for Eldem, AEXSHE0010170 and Sedad Hakki gave only this lead and its sweep rows.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on Eldem: WebSearch naming the coded diary with cryptiana, Cryptologia and HistoCrypt returned only SALT records and a Schmeh post on another diary.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry treatment: known.py shows no GL.htm or Lasry row, and the WebSearch naming the diary with the cryptologic venues found none.
prior_art.edition: Decipherment in print, as excerpts: Edhem Eldem, 'Becoming Sedad Hakkı Eldem', essay in Serena Acciai, Sedad Hakkı Eldem. An aristocratic architect and more (Firenze University Press, 2018; open access, archive.org oapen-20.500.12657-55503, full text read), pp. 336-337 and notes pp. 349-350 and after, quotes the diary in English from May 1925 to October 1926. No full text is printed. The 2008 book by Tanyeli, Tanju and Eldem that assigned the AAE codes was not opened: only its press notice is open (SALT 199494).
prior_art.literature: Same essay: 'The coded diary Sedad Hakkı kept in 1925-1926' is cited from the 'author's collection', with AAE 064, 067 and 072 named (all within record 121243, AAE056-115); 38 lines of the OCR cite the coded diary. A grep of the text for decode, decipher and transcribe found no account of the system or of who decoded it. WebSearch found no cryptologic paper.

1889.key_check: No key seen or held. Edhem Eldem's quotations show the system was read by him or for him; the essay as grepped does not print it.
1889.duplicates: known.py on Eldem, AEXSHE0010170 and Sedad Hakki, and on 'Becoming Sedad' (no hits): only this lead and research/sweep_2026-11_ottoman_turkish rows; no catalogue entry or target holds the document.
1889.closed: Edhem Eldem's essay 'Becoming Sedad Hakkı Eldem' in Acciai 2018 (pp. 336-337, notes p. 349 ff.) quotes the coded diary of May 1925-October 1926 in English translation, citing AAE 064, 067, 072. Excerpts only, and the pages AAE038-054 are not cited individually, though they sit in the same notebook. The 2008 catalogue was not opened. Scans are Local Access at SALT, so the unprinted text cannot be worked remotely.

seen.where: Yale finding aid PDF for the Chlingensperg family diaries, GEN MSS 1495 (https://ead-pdfs.library.yale.edu/11037.pdf, read in full), with the Quicksearch list in Chrome (search.library.yale.edu/archives?q=Chlingensperg+encrypted). archives.yale.edu answers 403 in Chrome. No digital object is listed.
seen.extent: Series II, box 3, 1830 Schreib-Kalender volume: entries before 5 May in cipher; entries from 23 May to the end are the son's, in plain German. Number of cipher lines not stated.
seen.cipher: Finding aid, 1830: "This volume is partially encrypted with a cipher created by Joseph von Chlingensperg auf Berg. Entries prior to May 5th were written by Joseph von Chlingensperg auf Berg and encrypted in his cipher." Its note lists no decoded passages for this volume, unlike 1805-1811.

prior_art.decode: Ran known.py on the harvested DECODE dump for Chlingensperg, Chlingensperg auf Berg and GEN MSS 1495: no DECODE record, only this lead, the Beinecke sweep rows and removed sibling volumes 812 and 813.
prior_art.tomokiyo: No cryptiana page on this diarist: WebSearch for Chlingensperg with cryptiana and Tomokiyo returned only other encrypted diaries.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm row: the same WebSearch naming Lasry and HistoCrypt gave nothing on Chlingensperg, and known.py shows no Lasry row.
prior_art.edition: No edition of the diaries found (searches on 'Tagebuch', 'Geheimschrift', Bavaria). The only full decipherment on record is of another year: a 33-page cipher translation of the 1811 volume, box 2, unpublished as far as found.
prior_art.literature: The finding aid says the cipher 'has since been cracked by multiple sources' and that passages are decoded in notes in select volumes, naming 1805-1811-era volumes. Searches with Jonathan Hill, Schmeh and Beinecke found no article or dealer description; nothing records a reading of the 1830 entries.

1894.key_check: No key held in this repo and none tested: the volume is not online. The solved system exists at Yale (see key_held), so reading the cipher entries needs a scan, not a break.
1894.key_held: Not held here. At Yale: 1805 volume has notes on cipher translation, with two sheets on decoding in the 1801 volume, and the 1811 translation in box 2; the finding aid says multiple sources cracked the cipher. Untested on 1830.
1894.duplicates: known.py on Chlingensperg, Chlingensperg auf Berg, GEN MSS 1495: no catalogue entry or target for the 1830 volume. Other years 1805 and 1825 were entries 812 and 813, removed 2 Nov 2026; they are separate volumes.
